Database.//: Provider is Sqlite or Oracle. For production set Provider=Oracle and supply a real ConnectionString (e.g. via environment variable Database__ConnectionString or a secret store). Seed must be false against a real database.
Database.//Sequences: Per-table Oracle sequence overrides for names that don't follow {id_column}_seq. Each value was confirmed to exist in ALL_SEQUENCES on the live DB (2026-07-24) — a missing/misnamed one is ORA-02289 on the first insert, which SQLite CI can't catch. error_evt/return_scrap_item/sheet_skid_dimension_check/coil_ownership_transfer were added after the write paths were validated against the live .230 DB.
Database.//MaxIdTables: Tables whose id is assigned MAX(id)+1 (no Oracle sequence) — the legacy behaviour. The security admin tables have no *_id_seq in the legacy schema (PB assigned user_id/group_id/application_id via MAX+1), so listing them here avoids ORA-02289 on create. The AbisSchema-provisioned tables (sales-quote + abis_* owned tables) create NO sequence, so every one that assigns its id via NextIdAsync must be listed here or it 500s on Oracle (ORA-02289). abis_truck_appointment is the concrete case; abis_scheduled_job/abis_job_run currently use inline MAX+1 but are listed for safety.

Board.//LineOrder: The floor board's card order, by line_num, as the plant reads the floor (BL 84, BL 78, BL 110, BL 108, BL 36, BL 24 — user 2026-08-04). It is not numeric, alphabetical or activity-based, so it lives here rather than in a sort() a later reader would 'correct' into ascending. A line NOT listed still appears, after the listed ones.
Board.//DecommissionedLines: Lines that no longer exist on the floor (line_num). BL 60 = 3, decommissioned 2026-08-04; 3 is its real code on the live LINE table (verified on .230). Kept SEPARATE from LineOrder on purpose: forgetting to list a line in the order must not hide it. TWO effects: such a line drops off the floor board, AND it refuses NEW work — no new job, shift or downtime instance can be booked to it, and the DAS operations that assign work (current-job, current-coil, shift/start, coil-run/start, change-job, queue) answer 409. History is untouched: BL 60 carries 1,163 jobs on live and every one keeps saying so, the lookup still returns the line, and editing an existing record on it still works. Winding down stays available too — shift/end, coil-run/end, reverse and queue removal are NOT blocked, because BL 60 left 9 open shift rows and a queued job behind and that state has to be clearable.

//LabelPrinters.PlantMap: The real plant map (probed 2026-08-05), for whoever wires this up. SHIPPING 6x10in: 192.168.10.53 is a ZT620 at 300 dpi -> ^PW1800/^LL3000. SKID+SCRAP 4x6in, one printer PER LINE: BL78 192.168.9.14 (ZM400, 203 dpi -> ^PW812/^LL1218), BL84 192.168.9.15, BL110 has TWO - skid 192.168.9.9 and offload 192.168.9.11. Only BL78/BL84/BL110 are networked lines, so BL108/BL36/BL24 have none. HANDHELD receiving guns 192.168.10.8/.9/.10 pair with their own small printers 192.168.10.12/.13/.14 (from the legacy CGI). The Xerox units at 192.168.9.70/.71 are PAPER printers for BL78/BL84 - not ZPL targets. All Zebras are thermal transfer, so bodies must emit ^MTT.
//LabelPrinters: Shop-floor Zebra printers, raw ZPL over TCP. Empty Printers = the NoOp transport, which reports UNREACHABLE and therefore mints nothing (the safety property: no ABC number is drawn for a label that was never printed). Name -> 'host' or 'host:port'; the port defaults to DefaultPort. DefaultPort is 9100, the Zebra raw-socket standard, NOT legacy's 6101: measured on the plant network 2026-08-05, the 6x10 printer (192.168.10.53) answers on both 9100 and 6101 but the 4x6 (192.168.9.14) answers on 9100 ONLY, so hardcoding 6101 would make it permanently unreachable and block minting. DeviceRouting maps a scanner's source address to a printer name so a gun prints at the station beside it (legacy routed 192.168.10.8/9/10 -> .12/.13/.14); DefaultPrinter covers anything unrouted.

LabelPrinters.//LineRouting: Production line -> printer, for tags that come off a LINE rather than a scanner gun. Key is '<lineNum>' or '<lineNum>_<purpose>'; the purpose-specific key wins. USE UNDERSCORE, not a colon: the server configures this via systemd EnvironmentFile (/etc/abis/abis.env) where the key becomes an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE NAME, and a colon is not valid in one - systemd skips the line silently, so the printer ends up unconfigured while everything looks set. A colon is still accepted for appsettings.json deployments. BL110 has TWO printers, so it needs both forms. line_num is an internal CODE, not the BL number - resolve it from the LINE table (see GET /lookups/lines). Example: { '4': 'bl78', '7': 'bl84', '6': 'bl110-skid', '6_offload': 'bl110-offload' } - line_num 4=BL78, 7=BL84, 6=BL110 on the live LINE table with Printers { 'bl78': '192.168.9.14', 'bl84': '192.168.9.15', 'bl110-skid': '192.168.9.9', 'bl110-offload': '192.168.9.11' }. An unrouted line prints NOWHERE by design - a skid tag at the wrong line is worse than no tag.

Documents.//TheoreticalWeightCustomers: Customers billed on THEORETICAL weight, so the combi form's net column carries prod_item_theoretical_wt instead of prod_item_net_wt. Legacy hard-coded customer_id = 2802 (TOYOTA TSUSHO AMERICA, 50 shipments on live) into four of its combi sheet-detail DataWindow queries. It is a commercial arrangement, so it lives here rather than in SQL — a customer joining or leaving it is a business change, not a code change.

ApiKeys.//: Supply keys via configuration/secret (e.g. ApiKeys__Keys__0). Set Enabled=false only on a trusted internal network.

Scheduler.//: Scheduler EXECUTION engine. OFF by default (the /admin/jobs registry stays view/define only). Even when Enabled=true it ONLY runs allowlisted in-process operations (noop, heartbeat, …) — there is no shell/legacy path, so it can never fire the legacy EDI/cron work (single-owner guardrail). Set Enabled=true only after adding the operations you actually want scheduled.

WinSpc.//: Read-only connector to the plant WinSPC (SQL Server) quality DB on RSEDAM-PC (192.168.10.143, static TCP 1433). Disabled by default. To enable: set Enabled=true and supply a read-only ConnectionString. Recommended (good-citizen on the live SPC box): WinSpc__ConnectionString='Server=192.168.10.143,1433;Database=WinSPC;User Id=abis_ro;Password=...;TrustServerCertificate=True;Connect Timeout=5;Max Pool Size=5'. Provider=Sqlite is for the test mimic only. Job/Coil tag patterns match WinSPC's free-text tag names. CommandTimeoutSeconds caps any single read.

Audit.//: Set Enabled=false when the target schema has no compatible audit table (the live DBO schema has no opc_action_log). Otherwise auditing self-disables after the first write failure.

Email.//: TEST PHASE: OverrideRecipient redirects EVERY email (automated/triggered/manual) to this one inbox — real recipients are preserved in the subject/body. Clear it (empty) ONLY at the production cutover. Smtp.Host empty = log-only (nothing sent); set it to the plant relay to actually deliver.
Email.//SendTestOnStartup: Set true (e.g. Email__SendTestOnStartup=true) to send one diagnostic email through the full pipeline at startup — a deploy-time smoke test. Logs the redirect when Smtp.Host is empty; delivers once the relay is set. Default off.
